A1.justification: Both PDFs describe V²-SAM and contain readable main text, equations, references, and supplementary material. All 19 pages in each version support comparison, including the tables and qualitative figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on Ego-Exo4D, DAVIS-2017, and HANDAL-X, plus component ablations, expert-selection analyses, and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results and supplementary experiments, including the ablations and runtime comparisons.

M1.justification: The anchor and visual prompt generators, three experts, training losses, and PCCS inference procedure remain unchanged. Figure 2 expands their illustration, and Section 3.3 adds hats to quantities already described as predictions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Ego2Exo and Exo2Ego tasks, DAVIS-2017 correspondence evaluation, and HANDAL-X transfer setting. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3, including Ref-SAM, ObjectRelator, O-MaMa, and the DAVIS correspondence baselines. The supplementary Cycle-Mask versus Cycle-Points comparison is also retained.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, 20-frame DAVIS gap, HANDAL-X zero-shot setting, and training configurations remain unchanged. Supplementary Tables 6–8 retain the same dataset statistics and settings.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same individual-expert, expert-combination, submodule, anchor-count, and PCCS ablations. Scene-specialization and qualitative consensus analyses are retained; their relocation does not add evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its experimental results.

E6.justification: Result entries in Tables 1–5 and 9–11 are unchanged. These include 48.0 total IoU on Ego-Exo4D, 78.8 J&F on DAVIS-2017, and 77.2 IoU on HANDAL-X. The qualitative predictions are also retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, losses, and correspondence formulations remain unchanged. Adding prediction hats in Section 3.3 clarifies notation without introducing different mathematical reasoning; no proofs or formal assumptions are added.

C1.justification: The first contribution qualifies the novelty claim from the first framework adapting SAM2 to the first unified framework that architecturally adapts it. The abstract, remaining contributions, and three-benchmark state-of-the-art claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations of expert complementarity, sparse-anchor effectiveness, PCCS efficiency, and cross-view generalization remain the same. No substantive new limitation, failure condition, or applicability qualification is introduced.

D1.justification: The abstract's project link changes from v2sam.space to jianchengpan.space/projects/V2-SAM/. Both versions still promise future code and model release; the PDFs do not establish changed availability. Implementation and reproducibility settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 reorganizes cross-view methods into matching-based and learnable model-based paradigms and explicitly contrasts V²-SAM's coordinate cues with ObjectRelator. It removes the detailed long-term-memory discussion while retaining that citation elsewhere. The Boot et al. and Hadsell et al. references are removed.

P1.justification: The cross-view related-work passage is rewritten, with smaller edits to contribution wording, contact information, capitalization, notation, and captions. Bibliographic entries are shortened, while the main and supplementary section structures remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn to show training-only supervision, loss terms, and explicit expert outputs. Figure 1 is reformatted, table typography changes, and several supplementary tables and figures move between pages. All 11 tables and 14 figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The revised Figure 2 makes the existing training supervision and expert-selection flow easier to follow. Section 2 clarifies research positioning, and Section 3.3 improves prediction notation. These provide limited explanatory gains, while the method, experimental support, and most reproducibility information remain unchanged.
